newsitem.title: INDIA: India Congress regrets failure to protect mosque.
newsitem.headline: India Congress regrets failure to protect mosque.

text.p: India's Congress party on Friday said it regretted its failure to protect a mosque which was torn down by Hindu zealots in 1992 and blamed Hindu nationalists and their allies for the incident.

The demolition of the 16th-century Babri Masjid in the northern town of Ayodhya in December 1992 ignited two months of Hindu-Moslem clashes in which more than 3,000 people died in the worst sectarian violence to hit India since the subcontinent's bloody partition in 1947.
The mosque incident was widely perceived to have undermined Congress's traditional Moslem support and played a significant part in the party's rout in general elections in May 1996.

"The Congress party once again condemns the act of vandalism perpetrated by the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and its allies in destroying the Babri Masjid by throwing to winds all canons of civilised behaviour and ignoring its own commitment to the highest judiciary of the land, the parliament, to government and national integration council," the Congress party said in a resolution.
"The Congress also regrets its inability to carry out the legal responsibility in protecting the Babri Masjid," the party's political resolution said.

A BJP-led government in the state of Uttar Pradesh, in which Ayodhya is situated, had assured the federal Congress government headed by former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao that it would take steps to protect the mosque but failed to do so.
"We believed certain parties. We should not have done so," senior Congress leader Santosh Mohan Deb told reporters.
"Thereby constitutional obligations were not fulfilled properly," Deb said.
Rao's Congress government in early 1993 dismissed four state governments led by the BJP and banned two Hindu organisations that formed the backbone of the BJP's mass support.
